column4: אֶהְיֶה is imperfect (incomplete), first person: "I will be", as in 3:12 (אֶהְיֶה עִמָּךְ, "I shall be with you"); the ULT's "I AM" renders it as present.
הֱיוֹת־אֶהְיֶה is the infinitive absolute with the imperfect of הָיָה, the emphatic "I would surely be", not the name; the ULT's "the being of I AM" reads אֶהְיֶה as the name of Exo 3:14.

וַתְּדַבֵּר is the Piel of דבר, used here once outside speaking: she imposed her will on the royal seed, as the Hiphil subdues peoples under someone (Psa 47:4), and made it permanent by putting them to death (22:11). The ULT's "destroyed" brings in אִבֵּד from the parallel 2Ki 11:1.
